Subject: Proposed contract edits — data handling addendum attached

Dylan,

Thanks for the demo last week — Clearwave is excited about the latency profile you showed. We've circulated the standard contract through procurement and legal and attached a redline (v3) with a few asks that are blocking our security review. High-level items: 

- Telemetry & inference metrics: request to remove per-token/session telemetry being retained offsite. We asked to limit telemetry to aggregated metrics and only store traces for 14 days.
- Subprocessors: require a published, fixed list of subprocessors and 30 days' notice for additions (no broad all-subprocessors language).
- KV cache / model cache retention: carve out that any cached customer content be purged within 7 days and not used for model training.

I've attached the redline PDF and a short spreadsheet summarizing the clauses. Procurement would like Product and Security to review and provide a consolidated position or alternative language by EOD Thursday so we can move to signature.

Claire Zhou
Contracts & Procurement 
Clearwave Health

Thanks for flagging this, Dylan. Quick Product view: 

- Telemetry: we can offer aggregated telemetry (RPS, 95p latency, error rate) with per-tenant traces retained for 14 days. Removing all per-token telemetry would hurt our ability to debug production incidents; propose language that limits retention to 14 days and allows on-demand export with customer approval.

- KV/cache purge: for requests routed to our hosted service, we can guarantee TTL-based automatic purge at 7 days for customer-specific KV snapshots if the customer elects the 'data-ephemeral' configuration. Note: this requires them to accept a small perf delta because we rely on prefix caching to avoid repeated decoding. I can quantify the perf delta if they need. For Dedicated/Private deployments we need to be explicit: Dedicated can meet 7-day purge for managed caches; Private (on-prem) is customer-controlled.

- Subprocessors: Product side is neutral; this is more of a legal/comms ask. From an operational standpoint we can provide a published list of primary infra partners (GCP us-west3, S3 backups through PartnerX) and a 30-day notice is workable for non-emergency changes. We cannot promise no future additions, but we can commit to a notification+objection window and an emergency-change fallback with a minimum of 72 hours' notice for incident-related swaps.

Suggested compromises to propose back to Clearwave: 
1) Telemetry: aggregated by default; per-tenant traces kept 14 days; additional traces available on request under a support process.
2) KV/cache: offer 'data-ephemeral' opt-in with 7-day purge; note perf delta and list Dedicated/Private exceptions.
3) Subprocessors: publish current list in the contract and commit to 30 days' notice for additions except in documented emergencies.

If Legal/Security are okay with the wording, I think Procurement will accept. Happy to jump on a call with Claire to walk through trade-offs.

— Evelyn Hart
Product Manager, Inference Platform
Redwood Inference
From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
To: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai, evelyn.hart@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Mar 2027 14:38:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Fwd: Proposed contract edits — data handling addendum attached

Thanks Evelyn — those suggestions map well to what Legal/Security consider acceptable. A few Legal/Security edits I'm proposing to the vendor redline: 

- Telemetry: Accept aggregated telemetry & 14-day trace retention. Add explicit language that any exported traces require a Data Access Request (DAR) and must be approved by the account owner and Security. No retention for raw request payloads beyond the 14-day window.

- Training prohibition: Clear and absolute clause that customer content will not be used to train models outside of the parties' mutual written agreement; add audit rights with a 30-day notice window for a one-time audit per year.

- Subprocessors: Replace 'subprocessors and affiliates' catch-all with an appendix listing current subprocessors. Add a clause: Redwood will notify the customer 30 days before onboarding any new subprocessor; customer may object in writing and seek mitigation; in emergencies Redwood may onboard for up to 14 days while mitigation is implemented.

- Remedies: we should avoid open-ended indemnities. Propose liquidated damages cap aligned to the MRC and measured incident impact. Legal will provide exact redline text.

If Product wants to quantify perf delta for the ephemeral purge option, please send numbers and I'll include them in the redline as an explicit customer trade-off note. Assuming Product numbers are provided, Legal can produce a consolidated redline to send to Clearwave.

Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel, Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference
From: dylan.brooks@redwood.ai

Subject: RE: Proposed contract edits — data handling addendum attached

Claire — thanks for the redline and patience while we reviewed. Attached is our consolidated position (we'll upload the redline PDF to your Drive link). Summary of agreed points: 

1) Telemetry: Redwood will provide aggregated telemetry by default (RPS, latency percentiles, error rates). Per-tenant traces will be retained for 14 days; exports require a Data Access Request approved by the account owner and Security.

2) KV/cache & training: We will offer a 'data-ephemeral' configuration which, if selected, will purge tenant-specific caches within 7 days. We documented a measured performance impact (~6-12% higher median latency for small requests) in the attached sheet. For Dedicated/Private deployments, purge behavior will be documented per-deployment and may be customer-managed. Customer content will not be used to train models without written agreement.

3) Subprocessors: We attached an appendix listing current subprocessors and commit to a 30-day notice period for new subprocessors, except in emergencies (72 hour notice where feasible; temporary 14-day onboarding for critical incident response).

Olga and Evelyn have signed off on the language from Product and Security. Please confirm if these compromises are acceptable and we'll circulate a final redline for signature. Happy to set a short call if you prefer to walk through details.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
